body.zh-HK:
> 面試官問：「點解 voice assistant 的 first-audio latency 唔可以只用文字 model 的 first-token latency 解釋？」
>
> 答啱一半嘅答案：「因為語音比文字大。」

人講完一句後，系統要先判斷佢係咪真係講完（endpointing），把聲音上傳並轉成文字（ASR），整理要交畀語言模型嘅資料（context），等語言模型（LLM）開始生成，最後把文字轉成聲音（TTS）。所以人等緊嘅，唔係 model 第一粒 token，而係自己講完後幾時聽到第一段有用聲音。由講完到聽到第一段有用聲音，時間會經過 endpointing、audio 上傳、ASR partial、context 組裝、LLM first token、TTS warm-up、第一個 audio frame 同 network buffer。任何一段慢、誤判人未講完，或者錯把背景聲當說話，體驗都會變差；文字 model 好快都補唔返。

## 先定義使用者真正感到的時間

把量度分開：turn-end-to-first-audio、turn-end-to-final-answer、barge-in-to-silence、ASR partial-to-correction 和 TTS cutoff rate。每個 metric 要說清起點和終點，否則一組可以邊播邊生成的系統，會和一組等完整轉寫才開始的系統被錯誤比較。也要分 traffic slice：短句、長句、繁中和英文夾雜、較嘈的 audio、cache warm／cold，以及需要 retrieval 的 request。

## 拉一條完整聲音 trace

為每一 turn 記 VAD start/end、ASR first/final hypothesis、context ready、LLM first/final token、TTS first/final frame、stream interruption 和 fallback。當 first-audio 高，先看 endpointing 是否等太久、ASR 是否在重試、TTS 是否冷啟動，或 LLM／retrieval 真是瓶頸。若 average 快但少數人被長靜音或錯誤 interruption 困住，p95／p99 和 error replay 才揭示真正問題。

## 速度不可以壓過理解和同意

可以用 partial ASR 提早開始，但要規定哪種意圖不可在未確認轉寫前做出結論；例如含日期、數字、名字或 code-switching 的指示，可先播一個短確認，再把後果性步驟交回人手。錄音或音訊保留要先講 consent、用途、存放與刪除；synthetic audio demo 不應假裝已處理真實使用者聲音。較短 silence 有價值，但不是叫系統猜快一點。

## 用可控 audio fixture 測整條路

建立短句、長句、中英夾雜、背景噪音、停頓、interrupt 和無法辨識的 synthetic audio fixtures。對每條定 expected transcript range、可接受 first-audio budget、是否可被打斷、以及何時要向 user 澄清。比較 candidate 和 baseline 時，同時報 latency、transcript correction、handoff、cutoff 和被拒絕的 high-risk action。這證明你在優化對話，而不是單獨壓低一個模型數字。

## 面試時的一句清楚回答

『我會把 first audio 拆成 VAD、ASR、context、LLM、TTS 和 network budget，按使用者可感到的起點量度。改善其中一段前，我會確認它不增加誤轉寫、打斷失敗或未確認的決定。』這句包含機制、取捨和驗證方式。

## 讓設計可被審閱

- **工程：** stage trace、audio-fixture manifest、per-slice latency table、barge-in test 和 fallback contract。
- **交付：** consent 文案、不可自動處理的 intent、何時請 user 重講、誰接住低信心 turn。
- **風險：** 一個更快但錯聽數字或姓名的案例，說明為何最低 latency 不是唯一目標。

## 延伸閱讀

[平均快咗，P99 可以更差](/zh-HK/interview-lab/a-faster-average-can-hide-a-worse-p99)、[Token budget 唔等於識處理多語內容](/zh-HK/interview-lab/token-budget-is-not-a-language-test) 和 [加大 model 前，先做 gradient check](/zh-HK/interview-lab/a-gradient-check-precedes-a-bigger-model)。

## 範圍說明

這是 AI.DOG 的單題練習。audio、transcript、consent 和 metrics 均為 synthetic 教學材料；它不處理或代表真實錄音、用戶同意或產品服務。

body.en:
> Interviewer asks: “Why can’t a voice assistant’s first-audio latency be explained only by a text model’s first-token latency?”
>
> Half-right answer: “Because audio is bigger than text.”

A person is not waiting for the model’s first token. They are waiting to hear useful sound after they finish speaking. That silence includes endpointing, audio upload, ASR partials, context assembly, LLM first token, TTS warm-up, the first audio frame and network buffering. A slow stage, a false decision that the person has not finished, or background sound mistaken for speech all damage the experience; a fast text model cannot repair it.

## Define the time a person actually feels

Measure separately: turn-end-to-first-audio, turn-end-to-final-answer, barge-in-to-silence, ASR partial-to-correction and TTS cutoff rate. Define each start and end point, or a system that can speak while generating will be compared incorrectly with one that waits for a final transcript. Slice traffic too: short and long utterances, Traditional-Chinese/English code-switching, noisier audio, warm/cold cache and requests requiring retrieval.

## Draw the complete audio trace

For every turn, record VAD start/end, ASR first/final hypothesis, context ready, LLM first/final token, TTS first/final frame, stream interruption and fallback. When first audio rises, check whether endpointing waits too long, ASR retries, TTS cold-starts, or LLM/retrieval is actually the bottleneck. If the average is fast while a minority experience long silence or faulty interruption, p95/p99 and error replay reveal the problem.

## Speed cannot outrun comprehension and consent

Partial ASR can make a response start sooner, but define which intents cannot reach a conclusion before transcription is confirmed. A date, number, name or code-switched instruction may need a short confirmation first and a human for a consequential step. For audio recording or retention, state consent, purpose, storage and deletion first; a synthetic-audio demo must not imply real user audio was handled. Shorter silence is valuable, but it is not permission to guess faster.

## Test the entire path with controlled audio fixtures

Create synthetic audio fixtures for short and long utterances, language mixing, background noise, pauses, interruptions and incomprehensible speech. Define an expected transcript range, acceptable first-audio budget, interruptibility and the point at which the user needs clarification. Compare candidate and baseline on latency, transcript corrections, handoffs, cutoffs and rejected high-risk actions. That demonstrates optimisation of a conversation, not compression of one model number.

## One clear interview answer

‘I split first audio into VAD, ASR, context, LLM, TTS and network budgets, measuring from the moment the person experiences as the end of their turn. Before improving one stage, I check that it does not increase mistranscription, failed interruption or an unconfirmed decision.’ That sentence contains mechanism, trade-off and validation.

## Make the design reviewable

- **Engineering:** stage traces, audio-fixture manifest, per-slice latency table, barge-in test and fallback contract.
- **Delivery:** consent copy, intents that cannot be automated, when to ask a user to repeat, and who receives a low-confidence turn.
- **Risk:** a faster case that hears a number or name incorrectly, explaining why lowest latency is not the only goal.

## Further reading

[A faster average can hide a worse P99](/en/interview-lab/a-faster-average-can-hide-a-worse-p99), [A token budget is not a language test](/en/interview-lab/token-budget-is-not-a-language-test), and [A gradient check precedes a bigger model](/en/interview-lab/a-gradient-check-precedes-a-bigger-model).

## Scope note

This is an AI.DOG single-question practice exercise. Audio, transcripts, consent and metrics are synthetic teaching material; it does not process or represent real recordings, user consent or a product service.
